header: I want to be polite to the embedding service when the archive re-read applies hundreds of vectors. The first apply of the whole archive hit "429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" on the five heaviest circulars (50-75 chunks sent in a rapid burst); the tool left them untouched, but it should not need a second manual run. So: throttled() spaces the calls out (one at a time, at least minIntervalMs apart) memoized() remembers a vector already computed, so a retried circular does not pay for the same chunk twice applyWithQuotaWait() if the service refuses on quota, WAIT for the per-minute window to clear and try the circular again; if it still refuses after the waits, say so (quotaExhausted) so the run can stop instead of burning time. All time-dependent parts are injectable, so I test this without waiting.

symbols.name: realClock
symbols.sig: const realClock: Clock = { sleep: (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)), now: () => Date.now() }

symbols.name: throttled
symbols.sig: export function throttled(embed: EmbedFn, minIntervalMs: number, clock: Clock = realClock): EmbedFn
doc: I make the calls one after another, never closer together than minIntervalMs.

symbols.name: memoized
doc: The same text is embedded once, and I do NOT remember a failed call.

symbols.name: isQuotaError
doc: True for a rate-limit / quota refusal, as opposed to a real error such as a bad key.

members.name: quotaExhausted
doc: Set when the service still refused on quota after every wait: more circulars would only fail the same way.

symbols.name: applyWithQuotaWait
symbols.sig: export async function applyWithQuotaWait<T>( fn: () => Promise<T>, opts: { waitsMs: number[]; clock?: Clock; onWait?: (waitMs: number, attempt: number, total: number) => void },): Promise<QuotaWaitResult<T>>

params.name: opts
params.type: { waitsMs: number[]; clock?: Clock; onWait?: (waitMs: number, attempt: number, total: number) => void }

doc: Runs fn; on a quota refusal it waits waitsMs[0], retries, then waits waitsMs[1], ... I return any other error at once and never retry it.

behaviours: the real Google 429 message is recognised as a quota error
'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED' and 'rate limit' alone are recognised too
a bad key, a network error or a database error is NOT a quota error
calls are at least 1000 ms apart (the first goes at once)
no needless waiting when enough time has already passed
calls made at the same moment still run ONE AT A TIME, in order, and each gets its own answer
a failed call does not block the next one
the same text is embedded once
a FAILED call is not remembered: the next attempt really tries again
two quota refusals, then success: it waited 65 s twice and the circular was applied
still refused after every wait: it gives up, says quotaExhausted, and made exactly 3 attempts
a real error (bad key) is returned AT ONCE: no waiting, no retry, and it is not called 'quota'
success on the first try waits for nothing
6 chunks, refused at the 4th: after the wait only the 4th, 5th and 6th are requested again (7 API calls, not 10)
